newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly higher.

text.p: NY precious metals ended mostly higher Friday, as the complex recovered partially from Thursday's weakness with help from a sliding stockmarket, but the weakness in the U.S. dollar continued weigh on gold in particular.

After COMEX closed the fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Average accelerated and the index ended down 247 points, its second biggest one day point drop ever, leaving the Dow down 6.8 percent from its all time high of 8259 seen on August 6.
Precious metals have received some support recently from investors worried about the potential for a significant stock market correction.

"There's been good buying of both gold and silver out of India recently, but the peformance of gold is not that impressive given the recent weakness in stocks and bonds," Merrill Lynch commodities research director, Bill O'Neill said.
"Gold lease rates remain high on borrowing by large funds looking to sell the market as they did six months ago and there's been some producer selling all week though not in big tranches," he said.

"We've not heard of any central bank selling, but central banks remain heavy lenders and there's constant overhead pressure from producers as given the low price of gold its incumbent on producers to hedge to remain profitable," he said.
COMEX December gold ended up $1.50 at $329.50 an ounce, after recovering from Thursday's low at $326.60. COMEX estimated volume was 32,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $325.80/30 an ounce, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $324.65 and the New York close Thursday around $324.20/70.

Implied gold lease rates have risen sharply in the past three days and are now at their highest levels since January with the forward curve inverted, suggesting funds may be re-establishign short positions, traders said.
One month gold lease rates were around 2.73 pct early Friday, up from 1.81 pct last Friday, with the one year rate around 2.32 pct, up from 2.14 pct last Friday.
COMEX September silver ended up 15.5 cents at $4.56 an ounce, its highest level since early July. COMEX silver volume was estimated at 25,000 lots.
COMEX silver open interest rose 1,154 lots Thursday, after a large rise in open interest Wednesday, with silver looking stronger than gold in the past few weeks.
The spot gold/silver ratio slipped to 71.29 at the close, from 73.25 Thursday and is now at its lowest level since late June, reflecting the relative strength of silver.
NYMEX October platinum ended down 30 cents at $427.50 an ounce, after recovering from a session low at $416.00, but back month in platinum ended higher.
NYMEX September palladium closed off $4.55 an ounce at $205.30.

"There were some wild swings in palladium, as it looked like Russians were selling, and once people heard the Russians were selling everybody looked to go short, but then a couple of dealers jumped in and started buying it up, so we saw a good $10 range in Europe which is pretty unusual," one refining source said.
